selection_criteria.predictive_performance: HGB edges LR on F1, PR-AUC, log loss, and Brier; LR remains competitive (ROC-AUC slightly higher).
selection_criteria.probability_quality: Both models have usable probabilities; HGB slightly better Brier/log loss. LR probabilities are still suitable for thresholding.
selection_criteria.business_value: Under default YAML costs, LR at threshold 0.15 yields higher holdout business value (~37k) than HGB at its BV-optimal 0.1 (~34k).
selection_criteria.interpretability: Logistic regression coefficients map to log-odds — preferred for an educational project.
selection_criteria.complexity: LR is simpler to train, explain, and deploy; capacity gains from HGB are modest here.

decision: Use logistic_regression with business-value-optimal threshold 0.15. This demonstrates that the best ML leaderboard metric does not automatically maximize business value.
false_positive_meaning: Customer predicted to churn who would have stayed — wasted retention offer cost.
false_negative_meaning: Customer predicted to stay who churns — missed intervention and lost customer value.
